paper.title: Analytic reproducibility in articles receiving open data badges at the journal Psychological Science: an observational study

judgement_checks.abstract_vs_body: Abstract: 9 (36% [20,59]) reproducible without author involvement; Results p.4: 9 (36% CI [19,57]) for the same quantity. Same n, same denominator (25), different CI bounds.
judgement_checks.claims_scan: claims_scan flagged Abstract 34% vs body; Table 1 gives 6 (24%, [8,47]) for the same cell, so 34% in the Abstract is not the value the code prints (24%).
judgement_checks.param_mismatch: Methods (Design p.3) say major = PE >= 10% and minor = 0% > PE < 10%; code preprocessing.R classifies via comparisonOutcome in data_values.csv (MATCH/MINOR_ERROR/MAJOR_ERROR) and manuscript.Rmd adds DECISION_ERROR to majorErrors. No numeric threshold in code; classification is pre-coded in the data file.
judgement_checks.figure_data_mismatch: Fig. 1 forest plot is built by meta_analysis.R from stored proportions; Fig. 3 valueTypePlot from data_values.csv valueType counts; no figure prints numbers that can be compared cell by cell.
judgement_checks.phantom_experiment: Paper describes a comparison sample of 30 articles without open data badges (Results p.4) and SI sections C/E; no data file or code for the 30-article comparison sample exists in materials (data/raw has only the 25-article corpus).

Confirm that both refer to the same quantity (same cohort, test set, metric) before keeping it.
